verdict.tagline: Rough technical issues plague a harsh survival MMO with deep building.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep survival base building
you can overlook sparse player populations
not_for_you_if: you will not install a third-party launcher
you want an offline single-player mode

claims.claim: The game lacks a local single-player option and requires connecting to servers to play.

citations.review_text: No single player option. Every other decent game like this allows you to just play locally without having to rent a server or some such this game does not allow that.

First of all it is NOT Singleplayer, it's a server game like Rust. When you want to play alone you have to buy your own server. Even on min. to max. graphic settings it runs like ♥♥♥♥, it stutters and breaks the grafic whenever you move to fast or even just try to turn around. The combat itself its meehh because of the wonky camara that has no problem to get stuck above your head and shows how bad your hairline looks when you get to close to an object. The melee combat is through the block function that only some times work or only triggers when it wants more luck based.
Online isn't fun when you're hunted. Single player is rent only with a monthly fee. I can't recommend this

I don´t see how this should be a singleplayer game.
You have to connect to servers.
Once there is a downtime, you can no longer play.
There are others players in your " Singleplayer game".

Yes, I read about the game before and I watched several videos.
But somehow I would have expected a selection bezween local singleplayer and multiplayer.

Beside this, at lease within the first 1,5 hours, the game feels like old  Call of Dutys with levels build like a pipe and everything is preselected and you are forced to play as the developers want it.

You want to build and just survive in the desert and find your space?#
Forget it, the developers want you to constantly kill everything, so you have to do so.

Enemies respawn faster that you can kill them.
Ths is simply due to the fact, that the wohle game is only build for multiplayer.
You fight your way along one of the pipe tunnels and once you reach the end, the enemies at the start are already back.

In addition, this is one of the first "singleplayer games" with latency problems...

This game is not bad, but the singleplayer flag is just a lie.
Unless it gets singleplayer I don't really care for it.

Why do they list it single-player game in the feature list? My first experience was to be forced to select a server so no solo option then secondly out of the tutorial you get a nice view of boxes everywhere the eye can see.
Other than that, the game looks great and the vibes were good.

I struggle with the features list saying single-player and then buying a released game and have to wait till september.
So just for that fact I can't recommend it. Nothing on the upper part of the store page indicates any of this well.

claims.claim: Players are forced to use the external Funcom launcher to start the game.

citations.review_text: This game wouldn't work no matter what I did. I couldn't get them game to launch correctly once let alone get past the shaders I tried every trick I could find ppl posting ab and nothing fixed it this game forcing the launch through funcom is stupid to say the least.

Update: I was finally able to get the game working.

Originally, I bought the game and could not get it to launch. 
It had been registered on my Steam account for over 24 hours, 
but every time I clicked Play, the Funcom Launcher opened 
and nothing happened when I clicked Launch.

I also tried opening the Account option in the launcher 
and signing in through Steam. The account page loaded, 
but it only showed me a link back to the Steam store, 
which made it look like the account was not properly 
recognizing that I owned the game.

After some troubleshooting, I got the game working by 
running the executables manually as administrator.

I ran these as admin:
DuneSandbox_BE.exe
This opened the game, but I eventually 
had to close it after it hit an error was not 
able to connect to funcom services.

DuneSandbox-Win64-Shipping.exe
After that, the game actually worked. :)

Testing it now to see how good it is. 
I am already loving the background music, 
the character creation, and the Discord people seem nice so far.👽

claims.claim: Reviewers state that connection instability results in server disconnect messages, forcing players back to the main menu and blocking access to menus or crafting while the error persists.

citations.review_text: Truly one of the more frustrating experiences I've had trying to play a game recently. The game requires you to be online at all times, even though I didn't see another player or do anything that would require multiplayer. I have gigabit internet service. If your connection destabilizes even momentarily, you get a massive "Connection to Server Lost" message, which remains on screen for something like a minute until it boots you to the main menu. Even worse, you can't actually do anything while this message is up; can't craft or access your inventory, not even quit the game. There is zero reason for you to be required to be online 100% of the time playing this game. In its current state it's unplayable.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires connecting to servers even when playing single-player mode.

citations.review_text:
Simply put: NOT FUN.

Single player requires joining a server (just because). Had to trawl through the region list to find server in a very different part of the world which has a "Standard" server to join (because none are in my region and none of it is automated or intelligent enough to find one by itself). Not interested in MMO, just want a good single player story campaign, wasted 30 minutes trying to figure out if I had started the wrong executable. I just want to download a game and play it, not spend time trying to work out if the game has falsely advertised a single player mode. There were no helpers along the way to explain that single player mode requires a server or why (really not an obvious move there devs - seems shifty to me, there are only a few reasons why you would want to join server for single player mode and all of them are great for the dev, but really not great for the user.) I'm not going to applaud it, it should be vehemently discouraged.

2 hours gameplay, trying to figure out the basic building mechanics (how to simply rotate an object so that its facing the right way) and I'm being constantly threatened with dehydrating to death. If you can't make the controls VERY VERY VERY obvious, then don't constantly threaten me with death when I know what to but can't figure out how to get your interface to do it, and a timely tutorial for basic construction controls seems non-existent (not sure why as fighting was quite well covered). I can handle death by Arrakis due to my own errors, it's a harsh planet, but to be given death due to the shortcomings of the UI is a MAJOR turnoff.

This has become a whining chore of a game to play due to idiotic dev decisioning after just 2 hours. Major red flag. I'm taking it as indicative of how much dev interface decisioning will ruin what should have been an awesome story to come (which I've now chosen to never experience). Reloads just to work out controls utterly disruputing the immersiveness and flow of the …

There isn't a 'meh' button unfortunately. 

It's VERY choppy on midrange equipment (and this laptop runs Elden Ring REALLY well). It's very rinse and repeat.

I haven't played long but I'm not falling in love. Keep trying but it's buggy, laggy and boring. When I bought it it clearly said "Single Player" and it isn't. The reason I play games is to get away from people. 

Unimpressed

claims.claim: Reviewers describe encountering performance issues including crashes, severe lag, and freezing.

citations.review_text: Game crashes at launch and actually resets my PC. Checked all my programs and bios, everything is up to date. Some spike in GPU most likely. Considering I am running 32g ram and a 5070 while having my graphics limited by an ini prompt you would think it would run fine. Seems like the game is asking for too much to start, most likely an unnecessary amount.

- Official servers are laggy, you should play on localhost.
- FPS freezes
- Server-client desyncs
- The battles/moves with lag are impossible
- Self hosted is a Microsoft Azure nightmare: Hyper-V + Kubernetes
- Punishing respawn: you lost everything ( and you'll be happy ), even if it's not your fault for a sandworm faster than you.

Unfinished, must be replaced by "Beta Public Game" or "Pre release" on steam.
Don't spend your money on.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe item and equipment durability as overly punishing, noting that gear breaks or gets damaged quickly during standard quests and travel.

citations.review_text:
I've played a few PVE games before and I am a fan of Dune, so this sounded like a natural for me. In terms of atmosphere they nailed it.  But in creating the harsh atmosphere of Dune, I think the developers went too far. 

I went into one of the bigger early quests and died several times, but I persevered and finished the quest, in which I gathered a bunch of items needed to build a sandbike. But when I was finally done, I looked at all the items I had collected. They were all badly damaged by the damage I'd been taken and I realized what the game breaker for me was: the durability of everything. It's not so bad having your base degrade over time due to sandstorms and heat, But having stuff in your back degrade while you're adventuring? 
Too much. I went on another quest and took damage, and at the end, my clothing was damaged so badly I had to replace it all.

This is already a game with serious grinding, but having to grind to replace items damaged when you are just doing quests? Nope.

One important note for players who ignore this (and that's fine--this game just wasn't for me) and take the plunge. When you are eaten by a sandworm you lose ALL your equipment irrevocably. More grinding to replace it all.

I feel like this game should be retitled GRIND: The Awakening.

So let me start off with this game is cool. Dune is a great IP and I'm glad that this game exists to experience that.

But-
 
It just-

its just to sucks play.
Just straight up sucks.


The early game is not fun. Its tedious, and excessively grindy, and overall, it just runs like absolute dog-crap.
I'm running at around recommended pc specs, at the lowest graphics, and it just runs bad. Cutscenes just break, NPC dialogue almost crashes my game every time. 

The grind is just not fun. Its not fun to deal with. I came into the game wanting to fly a freaking ornithopter. And guess what. Almost 20 hours in, and I still don't have one. The only reason I played this long (at the time of this review) is because of that. Genuinely one of the most unfun experiences to any early game I've ever played.
Gathering the resources for ANYTHING is just so insane. 

There is no reason I need to spend 4 hours of resource gathering for a single weapon/tool. 

And don't say "Oh but snax, you just need to go to the spots for those resources," Yeah, I'm sure its fun with your thopter flying around and getting millions of items around the map. I've only NOW just gotten the mark 2 bike. 

And maybe it's just a genuine skill issue on my end, but its not fun spending 30 minutes to get to one spot on the map for one singular resource.

AND THE DURABILITY. 
It's just not fun to deal with! I'm fine with spending resources to fix my tools and vehicles, but it being "broke" is not fun. It would be fine if it didn't cost 15 iron ingots and 4 Emf Generators to make it again. 
If the durability just didn't lessen it would be perfectly fine.

The water and stats are fine, the water can drain maybe just a bit slower, because it just feels like its never full, and the health could be better with more regen.


Maybe I'll leave a better review if I get farther in the game, but so far, I'd say so far my experience with this game is a solid 4/10.

citations.review_text: I so want to like this game, but I keep ending up rage quitting after dying in combat.. the fighting is clunky, non intuitive and very frustrating with all its stuns where you just shrivel up and die as you cant flee, change weapons, heal yourself or what ever. Sad but AO was still FC's best game ever, want to buy a sequel.

Brand new to the game and have already found the quality of the game to be extremely poor. For a game that has been officially released for almost a year now you would think minor bug fixes would have been implemented.

Pros:

Dune Open World Game (absolutely love the Dune franchise)

Cons:

Rubber banding (Server Based):

Ping continually fluctuates  all over the place when in-game. I have been informed by other players that this is a confirmed feature of the game. 


Early game combat feels horrible: (hopefully combat gets better as game proceeds)

Because of fluctuating ping times and rubber banding, enemies close gap and stun you before you can switch from ranged weapon to melee weapon. Not sure if parry is available on ranged weapons, but the gap closers enemies perform early game always stun my character and not being able to parry an attack with the ranged weapon makes it kinda useless early game.

BUGS- I literally have 4 hours played and have had to go to the reddit forums already to find out why the Blood Purifier doesn't show up in the construction menu after you research it. After a full year of release you would think a minor bug like this would have been fixed. (Spoiler Alert- you need to log out an log back in after researching the Blood Purifier, to have it show in your construction menu)

Server Migration:

New players were allowed to create characters on servers that were closing! I am not sure why I was allowed to create a Character on a server that is shutting down in 7 days. I am not even sure where to find out what servers are remaining open. Someone posted a list in Discord, but I don't have permission to view the channel for some odd reason, even though I am fully verified in discord.

I am being warned after 4 hours of game time that I need to put all my items in my bags and use some kind of tool to save my base. At my level, I don't see an option to create the tool that saves my base and my inventory is way to small t…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game world can feel empty and lacks other players, making large areas feel more like a single-player experience than an MMO.

citations.review_text:
### Steam Review

I’m having a great time with Dune: Awakening. The progression feels rewarding, the survival mechanics work well, and I keep finding reasons to explore further.

My main complaint is the state of the world. Arrakis feels **too empty now**. I can spend a long time exploring without seeing another player, and the huge map can feel more like a single-player world than an MMO.

That is a shame because the game is clearly built around having other players around. Seeing bases, vehicles, activity, and other players would make the world feel much more alive.

I’m still enjoying the game a lot. I just wish there were more people in it.
That said, the actual game underneath it is excellent. If Funcom keeps adding content and giving players more reasons to interact with the world, i could play this for ages.

Highly recommended, just a shame such a huge world currently feels so empty.
Decent enough game, just feels a bit dead - barely see other players etc.

I thought there would be more story to the game, more questing and more players. Instead I find myself grinding away for intel and really hard to get mats.  Mostly mats because there's a lot of dying in the game (for me) and losing your stuff to sandworms.  I haven't met another player yet soO there's not a lot of mmo vibes on my end.  I feel like I'm playing a offline survival game really.  The character creation was more immersive than the general gameplay in my opinion.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the base building system as a well-done and enjoyable feature of the survival gameplay.

citations.review_text: Overall great game with great base building and story. my biggest problem is that there are base pieces that you can see in capitals that you don't get to work with that would probably make things flow generally better in your base.

I'm sad because this is a very good game in many ways. The universe is appealing and immersive, the base-building is very well-done. I don't mind some grind, this was a good balance. The reason I'm sad is because I was hoping for a good solo experience, and I found it just too difficult. I'm an experienced gamer, albeit with old man reflexes - but I've beaten Dark Souls and other "difficult" games through persistence and craftiness, so I'm no slouch either. I can see how the quests could be very fun in a group. They're designed for that. I'm talking about game-progression quests that unlock necessary crafting recipes - these aren't optional - death really hurts when you've got a long way back to your corpse, and chances are you won't make it and end up losing everything - I can see why it was designed this way, and if I was playing with friends all of these issues would be mitigated enough - but solo it's just too hard to be fun - for me. A gamer with higher skills and more experience may find the challenge to be exhilarating but for me it was just an exercise in frustration which is not why I like gaming.

First off i have never watched dune and never will...

Awesome game so far. I haven’t experienced a single bug, crash, lag spike or any other issue.

The scale is impressive some player bases are so massive they feel like landmarks and there is no pop in or lag like you would get with conan or ark. It also has one of the best building systems I’ve seen in a survival game.

There’s a ton of depth in the progression system and plenty of content to work through. It’s survival done right. My only real complaints are that fall damage feels a bit excessive, even if it’s realistic, stamina can feel too limited during combat, and the Water Wars DLC is pretty meh.

Overall, the game is immersive, rewarding, and just genuinely fun. It’s the first game in a long time where I’ve felt completely satisfied with my purchase.

For context, I’m only at the aluminium stage, so I still have a long way to go before endgame. There’s definitely a grind, but getting everything too quickly would make the game boring anyway.
Fun game. Big maps are well bult. Hours of building enterteinment.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the base building system allows players to construct large structures and includes a duplication tool, though using the tool can sometimes place a hologram without successfully moving existing items.

citations.review_text: I have had a really good time in this game. I like the direction the devs are going. The atmosphere is pretty straight on. The pace of the game seems to be about right. I had some delay as I manage to get my trike stuck and had to put a ticket in. They were ok responsive but was helpful. Got the bike unstuck by recalling it which wasn't aware I could using the tool. Not soon after that got ate by a worm.. Not even mad... I would recommend as its been awhile since a game was able to pull me in. Still trying to figure out how people are building these crazy shelters. The amount of material required is mind boggling. How does one have enough time to gather all that. Also, still trying to figure out how to move bases as every time I use the duplicate tool it just places a hologram but doesn't actually move anything. I know I'm doing something wrong but Ill figure it out. Did I mention how the game looks... Its pretty.

First off i have never watched dune and never will...

Awesome game so far. I haven’t experienced a single bug, crash, lag spike or any other issue.

The scale is impressive some player bases are so massive they feel like landmarks and there is no pop in or lag like you would get with conan or ark. It also has one of the best building systems I’ve seen in a survival game.

There’s a ton of depth in the progression system and plenty of content to work through. It’s survival done right. My only real complaints are that fall damage feels a bit excessive, even if it’s realistic, stamina can feel too limited during combat, and the Water Wars DLC is pretty meh.

Overall, the game is immersive, rewarding, and just genuinely fun. It’s the first game in a long time where I’ve felt completely satisfied with my purchase.

For context, I’m only at the aluminium stage, so I still have a long way to go before endgame. There’s definitely a grind, but getting everything too quickly would make the game boring anyway.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world feels empty and lacks other players.

citations.review_text:
### Steam Review

I’m having a great time with Dune: Awakening. The progression feels rewarding, the survival mechanics work well, and I keep finding reasons to explore further.

My main complaint is the state of the world. Arrakis feels **too empty now**. I can spend a long time exploring without seeing another player, and the huge map can feel more like a single-player world than an MMO.

That is a shame because the game is clearly built around having other players around. Seeing bases, vehicles, activity, and other players would make the world feel much more alive.

I’m still enjoying the game a lot. I just wish there were more people in it.
That said, the actual game underneath it is excellent. If Funcom keeps adding content and giving players more reasons to interact with the world, i could play this for ages.

Highly recommended, just a shame such a huge world currently feels so empty.
Decent enough game, just feels a bit dead - barely see other players etc.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the early and mid-game progression as heavily reliant on grinding resources with limited hand-holding during quests.

citations.review_text: It's Conan with guns, but the close combat is a bit tighter, and the story is less exaggerated from the source material. Some of the dialogue is cringey but you'll get that in action-RPG's, ya gotta cover that backstory somehow. Private servers is the way to go; I couldn't imagine playing this with rando's fogging up the place. Early game can be punishing - knowing is half the battle. Practice blade blocking with the low level mobs until it's instinctual, you will never not need it. One warning - there is not much hand holding in questing. Sometimes you will search through crowds of nearly identical people to find the one you can talk to. Sometimes you cannot repeat dialogue trees. Sometimes the McGuffin isn't obvious, and you will pixel hunt (think Mankirk's Wife). Good for RPG feeling, but annoying after a half-hour. The respawn speed can be a bit high on default and can't be adjusted as of 10Aug26, but it's not unmanageable. Fun in groups! Oh, and the enemy apparently has access to all the same skills and equipment you do, so don't be surprised when the first boss hands you your ass with a Bene Gesserit combo.

I thought there would be more story to the game, more questing and more players. Instead I find myself grinding away for intel and really hard to get mats.  Mostly mats because there's a lot of dying in the game (for me) and losing your stuff to sandworms.  I haven't met another player yet soO there's not a lot of mmo vibes on my end.  I feel like I'm playing a offline survival game really.  The character creation was more immersive than the general gameplay in my opinion.

If you want to endlessly farm resources for the goal of getting more, different resources, then this is the game for you! I really thought this would be a more interesting game with a fascinating story. It was not that. It was boring, almost too big, and quickly got monotonous. Really disappointed.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that melee combat involves fighting shielded enemies whose health and shields reset if they are not hit with consecutive heavy strikes, alongside staggering mechanics when facing multiple opponents.

citations.review_text:
who ever decided to work on the shield combat for this game, i hope you get cancer.

if you dont double power strike them consecutively their shield and HP resets, so if your fighting mutiple enemies with shield and u heavy strike one, and then heavy strike a different NPC and go back to heavy strike the first to finish them off its not going to work, melee combat staggering you is crazy when your fighting 9+ people doing that spider man meme where they all point at everyone in a circle but their stabbing you so its a constant stun lock.

If you plan on going 'solo' DON'T BOTHER at this stage.  

PvE combat is heavily weighted on the 'enemy' side (bullet/dart sponges) whilst you flail around like a windmill missing everything, sniper rifle is not much better than a spitwad and has the range of a bowling ball thrown over your shoulder, whilst the OPFO can REACH OUT and touch you from just about anywhere.  

Wait till September for the roleout and then check the comments before even then getting the game.

If I had my chance over again, I'd not have laid out any money and just waited, but as they say "Caveat Emptor".

Cheers

UPDATE:

TL;DR--  DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY, NOW OR LATER.
Combat is absolutely ♥♥♥♥ in PvE.  Enemies are bullet sponges, you wear tissue paper armor and get bum rushed everytime you engage more than 2 opponents and get no real chance of fighting back as your continuously 'stunned/staggered'.

You've been warned!

I can't believe i'm writing this - but, this game actually makes a lot of fun. We're group of three people and being a ton of fun playing this game - and this actually includes farming, building and shooting around. And looks like after around 50 hours, we're still pretty much at the beginning.

Sure, it is not perfect. But it is still enjoyable if you take it as a Survival-RPG and like farming and building, in an awesome setting like Dune is. There are quite some mechanics you recall from the films too, so big kudos for this.

A brief list:

+ Atmosphere is great. The worm looks cool. Until he gets you first time.
+ There is a self-hostable private server available. Much kudos for getting this a thing.

+ The game devs are dedicated to their game, and it got a lot of updates since release. Also September 2026 update is supposed to be a major one. However, it feels rare game devs committing that much for their game - even if it (I think?) didn't get as big as they probably hoped it to.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe losing character inventory, base structures, and vehicles entirely after encountering bugs where characters fall through the world or servers experience data loss upon logging back in.

citations.review_text:
Way too punishing. Made it to Tier 3 when I got ate by a worm. Lost everything. Starting over in survival games typically have a catch up mode when you're in the mid-late game. Not this. The amount of back and forth I'd need to do, 1 end of the map to kill the low level enemies since the T3 and up mobs will 1 shot me with everything lost... it'll literally take 15-25 hours at minimum to get T3 gear again and that's with zero fast travel, going back and forth over and over and over and over. No way that's even remotely fun. Deleting my character and starting fresh would likely be easier and faster. 

The worst part is, I fell through the freaking floor and a worm killed me as my character sunk through everything. Apparently this "happens sometimes" per the zone chat. 
So.... something that makes you lose ALL progress on your character outside of your base, can just randomly happen to you when crossing the dessert? Why the hell would anyone play this who values their time?!

Breaks my heart to write a bad review for Dune. It's my favorite sci fi universe. I've read all the books, even the crappy ones after Frank. I'm a dune fanboi, but even I got my limits.
Didn't play for a couple weeks. Logged in and all my stuff is gone. My base, bikes, everything. Uninstall. Dumb system that doesn't add anything to the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game suffers from technical instability, including random crashes during gameplay, server connection timeouts, and slow loading times.

citations.review_text: Loading time is so slow, minimap adds to the problem by adding more loading time, the game is glitchy and unreliable, and you have to restart it frequently (did I mention loading time)? Yeah, sure, "I dream of it" a game that doesn't take years off your life waiting for it to let you play.

A buggy mess. I have to treat this game like a bomb that will explode at any second. Firstly, when I'm loading into a server, there is a constant chance that it just refuses to load with "Request Timed Out", "Battleye version outdated", "Couldn't load character in time", or some other error. While playing, the game just... randomly crashes. No reason. Just crashes. And it has awful optimisation from my knowledge as my frame rate is always bad despite lowering graphics settings. So, yeah, this game is basically an energy-draining trap. Overall idea, really cool! I love the idea of Dune and everything about it. But it's so damn buggy... anyway, this game kinda sucks in terms of performance and cortisol balancing, but the gameplay and fighting concept is fun. I don't recommend this game, but I do feel that it can be fixed in some way, but I don't know how games work, so I can't put forward any suggestions on how to fix this game.
Edit: I can't even play this game anymore without it crashing.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the endgame experience becomes tedious, repetitive, and unrewarding.

citations.review_text: Really enjoyed storyline, fear of worm and gathering most materials. End game is tedious, long and unrewarding. At this time to max out 1 of 5 skill trees once you have completed main story would take literal months of your time due to the extreme timegating. You can complete 5 missions per day that take anywhere from 10-30 minutes and are the same missions over and over. It seems like developers are pushing for intentional burnout. Really fun survival game then suddenly monotonous repetitive grind to the top.

Game is fun in the beginning. Then it just becomes repetitive. Barely any PvP. Even on the populated servers most people are not going into the PvP deep desert since there isnt really a reward especially when risking expensive vehicles. Wanted to play the game at launch and the pvp is what actually brought me to the game. Unfortunately my graphics card at the time couldnt handle it and I had to refund till recently. Good news is if you are just looking for a endless farming simulator in the dune universe this is for you. If you want a decent end game experience that varies this is not for you. Want to PvP? Not for you. There is pvp that happens. But in order for you to know for a fact you are going to get a fight you need to more or less coordinate in a discord.

Overall, the game is pretty good. You really have to decide what you're in it for though. I have been playing it since server launch, have seen it's multiple evolutions since then. Many people are right, it's Arrakis type threatening feel has lessened quite a bit, even the worm is more of an annoyance now. I played mostly as a solo player, about 90% of my play time I would say. It was definitely more challenging to do it that way. Griefers, resource gate keepers, and the cheaters early on really hurt the feel of the game... hence why it has changed the way it has. I am still really enjoying it though.

You'll really enjoy the rich storyline, flying around in an orni, it's visually breath taking. If you ever wanted to explore some of the world of Dune then this is a fantastic game that does really well at that. Majority of the issues of the game for me I am able to look past, at the end of the day... no game is perfect, there are always going to be flaws. That is not to say they couldn't do things to make it better though. End game is grindy, kind of pointless and group dependent right now. PVE threat, especially in the Deep Desert where there is none essentially, needs to be heightened to bring back that Arrakis feel. Although, I could see that being tough to do well, could easily become another annoyance. 

PVP combat, for those that are interested, heavily broken based on what I have heard and the new T6 Graded gear system apparently makes it worse now. In my opinion, the PVP system has always felt more like a promotion to those who enjoy griefing others. Didn't seem like there was much of a point unless you wanted to ruin someone else's day. The one place that seemed like PVPing was doing kind of well were the testing station teams that would battle each other to get the schematics. I would have loved to see some other pvping options here. 

I don't want to make this too lengthy, so I would give this...8.5/10. Pretty good with areas of improvement.

One of the best games I've ever played until end game.  Still recommended for a full playthrough even if you don't stick with it for end game.  

End game does not feel purposeful. Needs something more meaningful such as territory control.  Currently the reward for 'winning' is a bonus to production or access to special items, but those advantages are for what purpose?  So that you can win the bonus again next month?  ehhhhh....  Needs complete rework / new concept.  Refining existing concept isn't going to bring this game back to life as an MMO.  If this had Albion / EVE elements for end game..... (takes off pants)

*edit* - I only just now watched the trailer for the engame revamps.  Actually not bad in terms of a PVE game where the MMO concept isn't super important.  Not sure that's the direction I wanted this to go as having a bunch of people around in a thriving world would be more exciting.  Anyhow, am starting a new char and doing a new playthrough with g/f and look forward to checking out the new end game feature from a PVE-only game perspective.

Great game. I have spent an insane amount of hours in this game (700+). The building mechanics are incredible. the exploration and survival mechanics are very in depth. yes, you have to think about water frequently but I honestly wouldn't say it feels like a burden when playing. 

My biggest problems are the following two things: it has an insane amount of small bugs. from vehicles rendering in the wrong color, or when other users fly by your base, depending on how large it is, the pieces of the base will disappear for a second almost letting your character fall through the floor.

Lastly, the end game... its gotten significantly better since release. the addition of the landsraad missions and the speciality traits/levels. its been great, but i do feel like I wish there was more end game variety. ive played each mission type on each of the levels an INSANE AMOUNT OF TIMES. at this point its just hour long runs into the Deep Desert for supplies or play one of the landsraad missions for the nth time.

I am complaining a bit but overall I do love the game and I am really hoping it continues to receive support and new content for years to come. you give me destiny 2 quantity of DLC and ill be a happy camper.

I love the game. It does a lot of things right however it does a lot wrong. The endgame is still absolutely terrible. The landsraad missions are very repetitive and unrewarding. The specialization system is a great addition but the way to get through the levels is just boring and unfun. The overland testing station which is  required for the endgame are just flat out annoying. SOme of them arent as bad as others. I find them very repetitive also and just absolutely annoying due to the mechanics they have. For example, the electric boss. He stuns you with his gun, he stuns you with his shield explosion thing (which he spams SOOOOOO much), the electricity in the room is very hard to predict and also stuns you. The radiation boss is a race against time because of the radiation buildup only to get worse when he starts opening up the radiation pools on the ground that take up 90% of the room and speeds up radiation build up all while spawning nonstop ads. The endgame consists of farming 3 main resources, farming boring landsraad missions, and farming annoying overland testing stations. Thats it. The repetitiveness an annoying mechanics make me just not want to play this game anymore and frankly i just cant recommend this game to someone because of this. If the annoying mechanics were fixed and tamed down then i could get over the repetitiveness and would change my review to positive.

For starters, game has very good atmosphere of survival and constant need to gather things just to keep on living, being always scared that you can become food for word etc. 
But, further away to middle game the grind intensifies, it becomes more and more tiresome, everything until tier 6 which involves a lot of farming spice, titan and more for a really long time without any change in gameplay for hours, before you can craft a crawler to ease your life for one.
This game is fantastic from early-game to mid-game, the late game is not for the most people

good game have almost 300hrs into it but i will say sword fighting in this game or even knife fighting is trash and seems like it still is and they havent fixed it so i would say dont choose the sword master is sucks and is stupidly jank

Overall, a great game and worth the money (Especially during a sale). The early and mid game are 11/10. It gets a bit grindy and repetetive towards the end game. But just playing up to that point is 100% worth it. Can't wait for more content.

Oh boy where to start... First they removed 2 story dlcs from season pass and added 2 cosmetic dlcs instead which i was not paying for.

The story was average and felt much like conan exile building wise. The progression is most of the content so dont expect much after it.

Endgame is empty now and the new landsraad system and recycled testion stations just feels like a chore to do. They did split up the Deep desert aswell so you got a pvp and a pve now. So if you buying it to get the "Arrakis experience" you wont since that is gone now. There no harsh or unforgiving stuff anymore or faction wars in Deep desert so it just a classic spice/titanium loot simulator now.

For solo players since they expect to be able to play solo in a "MMO" game which it aint anymore and its quite possible to solo it. They are working on a singleplayer version that will come 22 sept unless they change the release date.

Funcom had no backbone and chose the easiest development route instead making it an unique experience. But what we got now is just a game living on maintence mode being a chore simulator.

Save time and skip this one.

Great game. I have spent an insane amount of hours in this game (700+). The building mechanics are incredible. the exploration and survival mechanics are very in depth. yes, you have to think about water frequently but I honestly wouldn't say it feels like a burden when playing. 

My biggest problems are the following two things: it has an insane amount of small bugs. from vehicles rendering in the wrong color, or when other users fly by your base, depending on how large it is, the pieces of the base will disappear for a second almost letting your character fall through the floor.

Lastly, the end game... its gotten significantly better since release. the addition of the landsraad missions and the speciality traits/levels. its been great, but i do feel like I wish there was more end game variety. ive played each mission type on each of the levels an INSANE AMOUNT OF TIMES. at this point its just hour long runs into the Deep Desert for supplies or play one of the landsraad missions for the nth time.

I am complaining a bit but overall I do love the game and I am really hoping it continues to receive support and new content for years to come. you give me destiny 2 quantity of DLC and ill be a happy camper.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that base structures and character progress can be lost due to server closures, wipes, or decay mechanics.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to like this game and I did for parts of it.
I played about 300 hours and I came to the conclusion that this is not a game for solo players.
The grind is just too difficult and the game is just not balanced in this regard.
The last straw came when I lost everything I've been working on for 2 weeks in a storm. My mistake or not, it's just not a good time in general when a game is that unforgiving .

I've had a lot of fun playing this game when it first launched! I understand the reasoning behind all of the decisions made by the developers, even the controversial ones, but it's only one decision that destroyed the game: structure decay in the Eastern Shield Wall area. These bases should have been left intact and not affected by the Arrakis weather. This way, even if players left for a couple of months, they would have had the base intact when they came back.

Everything else could have been ironed out in time, if the player base was still there. But when you made the decision to take out our base, our vehicles and our hard-earned resources, what else did you expect to happen? All servers are empty, and my 5 friends haven't logged in since last year.

And even if I want to start the grind all over again, there is nobody to play the game with, and the bases are still going to decay, so what's the point?

If you haven't played the game yet, I would still recommend a playthrough, as long as the game is heavily discounted. The fights are mediocre and repetitive, some missions require a lot of wasted time doing nothing (the developers don't respect our time at all), if you have to leave the game in the middle of a mission or if you lose power/internet then you may be in trouble when you log back. This being said the co-op is really nice, if you have a friend to play with, the atmosphere is eerie and the desert is merciless, the base building is super fun and rewarding, and finally assembling your first ornithopter and taking out for a spin feels amazing!

I wish we wouldn't have to travel manually to Arrakeen and Harko Village. Having to fly to the edge of the map where we hit an invisible wall that teleports us to an interactive second map where we have to fly manually to these locations is simply annoying and pointless. That's a lot of wasted time for zero good reasons!

I wish we would be notified when a new player starts the game and be encouraged to team up from …

I had 400 hours in this game when Funcom decided to sundown the server I have been in since launch. After spending 3 hours preparing for and transferring my character to a new server, the land where my base was previously, is occupied in the new server/sietch. I am not going to waste anymore time dealing with game as a repercussion of a forced migration. Plenty of other games coming out to put my time into. Good luck to everyone else.

I have played this game quite a lot. But Funcom recently decided to close a lot of servers, including mine. They provided complex instructions how to prepare for character transfer. I did everything according instructions. However, when my character was transferred I lost everything including base which I had to be able to transfer, but I wasn't when I was placing it in new server. I wrote support regarding this issue, but no one have replied so far. So, I lost everything what I found and gathered during the game. Now I need to start over from the scratch. 
I don't recommend you to invest your time, because it could be wiped out if Funcom developers would decide to close you server.

claims.claim: Reviewers report experiencing server disconnections and client crashes during gameplay.

citations.review_text: This is a good game, when it isn't crashing. The number of crash to desktop events is getting increasingly frustrating. For it to be a year old and crashing so often is a hard knock against it. So, if it runs for you, you might get to enjoy it.
good game, disconetions are a killer in this game.

I am a fan of the Dune universe and looked forward to playing this game. I cannot recommend this game for long term solo experience. The newest update made the game even worse. Within the main story line and Hagga Basin, it is a great game. As soon as you have to go to the deep desert it becomes unbearably grindy (and that is with it being a grinding game anyway). Even entering a basic testing station for spice infused metals has become 30 minute battle against shield guys that seem to just take mag after mag as you kite them around a room. monotonous. Or sit there and fly several minutes between spice blows just to find 5 other guys scooping it up. I can spend an hour just trying to get enough for one large refinery load. Or spend hours getting the right unique schematics only to lag out in the middle of a flight and find out you have been eaten by worms when you log in (the only time I have ever been eaten by worms is lagging out and it has happened 3 times losing everything)I know they are making a single player experience but I would like to know why the game just keeps getting worse on the grind factor. It has such a good base game but they seem to try top add depth by adding cheap difficulty that just makes it take longer instead of adding any real depth to the game. I am not a new player. I played for a couple hundred hours just trying to get to the point where I felt like I could play the game without having to constantly go out and grind but nope. I am done for a while Dune. Good game in a lot of respects but don't start if you don't have hundreds of hours of your life you give it and I really can't recommend solo.
Game, when it works, is fun and arguably was worth the price of admission. The game crashing for the 100th time is not fun.
